page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 60 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 60 vCPUs, running at one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading (SMT). It features 240 GB of total RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). Each core has access to 32 KB of L1 data cache and 512 KB of L2 cache, supported by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. There are no included GPUs, and the server does not come with bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities, driven by the non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture. The system achieved a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 141,982.77, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances, complemented by strong multi-core Geekbench (17,297.0) and PassMark CPU (76,182.72) scores. In parallel workloads such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (520.43 GB/sec), software compilation via Clang (54,068.0), and Redis SET operations (86.31 million ops/sec), performance consistently falls into the top quartile. Single-thread performance benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (1,601.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (25.32 GB/sec), place in the middle 50%.

Tradeoffs for the t2d-standard-60 stem from its architectural optimizations and CPU feature set. While instruction extensions like AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, the instance lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Large-model CPU-based machine learning demonstrates these constraints; LLM inference text generation on a 70B parameter model falls into the bottom 10% at 2.56 tokens per second. Furthermore, large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth register in the median tier at 141.75 GB/sec and 64.61 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its high core count, absence of thread contention, and balanced memory allocation, the t2d-standard-60 offers strong resource efficiency for compute-dense parallel tasks. It is best suited for concurrent batch processing, continuous integration and software build pipelines, high-volume microservices, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise databases.
